key_insight: HCC-STAR is a clinically aligned large language model that turns EMR narratives into risk stratification, guideline-consistent treatment ranking, and individualized survival estimates for hepatocellular carcinoma.
clinical_relevance: It aims to reduce within-stage heterogeneity missed by standard staging systems and support faster, more accurate treatment decisions in HCC care.
method: Curated ~30,000 HCC cases from SEER and converted them into EMR-style narratives with clinician-validated prompt-based augmentation.
Built a knowledge-aligned reasoning framework with step-verifiable composite rewards to encourage guideline-grounded outputs.
Evaluated on a multi-center cohort of 6,668 patients from 12 hospitals in China against guidelines and competing models.
evidence_signal: In the abstract, HCC-STAR outperformed clinical guidelines and models including GPT-5 and Gemini-2.5 Pro on treatment recommendation and risk stratification, and was rated trustworthy by blinded hepatobiliary specialists.
watch_item: As a decision-support system, it still requires careful external validation, workflow integration, and oversight before real-world clinical deployment.
paper_title: Towards Precision Therapy in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Clinical-Reasoning LLM for Risk Stratification and Treatment Guidance
